name: Question 12
problem:
Find the solution to the initial value problem

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)={x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-{x}_{1}(t)+3{x}_{2}(t),\end{aligned}\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$
worked_solution:
First, we write down the matrix differential equation ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)$ for the given system:

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}]
$$

We need to find the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors of the matrix $A.$

- Since $A$ is lower-triangular, the eigenvalues are 

$$
{\lambda }_{1}=1\,\text{and}\,{\lambda }_{2}=3.
$$

- Let's go through the process of finding the eigenvectors.

- For ${\lambda }_{1}=1,$ we get 

$$
A-{\lambda }_{1}I=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we get an eigenvector 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

- For ${\lambda }_{2}=3,$ we get 

$$
A-{\lambda }_{2}I=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}]∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we get an eigenvector 
${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Now, we write down the general solution to the given linear system of differential equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={c}_{1}{v}_{1}{e}^{{\lambda }_{1}t}+{c}_{2}{v}_{2}{e}^{{\lambda }_{2}t} \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{3t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the values of ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}.$ Substituting $t=0$ into the general solution, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(0) & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\ {c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{0}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{0} & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}2{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{1}+{c}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{c}_{1}=1 \\ {c}_{1}+{c}_{2}=-3.\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equation, we get ${c}_{1}=\frac{1}{2}.$ Substituting into the second equation, we obtain ${c}_{2}=-\frac{7}{2}.$ 

Finally, we write down the solution to the initial value problem:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}-\frac{7}{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{3t}\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

First, we write down the matrix differential equation x′(t)=Ax(t) for the given system: [x1′(t)x2′(t)]=[10−13][x1(t)x2(t)]

We need to find the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors of the matrix A.

  • Since A is lower-triangular, the eigenvalues are λ1=1andλ2=3.

  • Let's go through the process of finding the eigenvectors.

    • For λ1=1, we get A−λ1I=[00−12]∼[1−200]. So, we get an eigenvector v1=[21].

    • For λ2=3, we get A−λ2I=[−20−10]∼[1000]. So, we get an eigenvector v2=[01].

Now, we write down the general solution to the given linear system of differential equations:

x(t)=c1v1eλ1t+c2v2eλ2t=c1[21]et+c2[01]e3t,c1,c2∈R

Next, we find the values of c1 and c2. Substituting t=0 into the general solution, we get the following:

x(0)=[1−3]c1[21]e0+c2[01]e0=[1−3][2c1c1+c2]=[1−3]

So, we have a system of linear equations {2c1=1c1+c2=−3.

From the first equation, we get c1=12. Substituting into the second equation, we obtain c2=−72.

Finally, we write down the solution to the initial value problem:

x(t)=12[21]et−72[01]e3t
